title: Speier et al. 2017 — A comparison of stimulus types in online classification of the P300 speller using language models
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from a P300 speller brain-computer interface study conducted by Speier et al. (2017). Ten healthy participants performed online P300 spelling tasks using a 6×6 character matrix with two stimulus conditions: famous faces and inverted faces. The dataset includes 32-channel EEG data sampled at 256 Hz, with approximately 1200 trials per training run across two sessions per subject, enabling investigation of stimulus type effects on P300-based communication systems.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a g.tec amplifier with 32 channels at 256 Hz sampling rate. The P300 speller paradigm employed a 6×6 character matrix with visual stimulus presentation (famous faces and inverted faces). Participants completed 2 sessions with 3 runs per session. Reference electrode was placed at the left ear with ground at AFz. Line frequency was 60 Hz.
